description:
The surah that opens by naming the occurrence of the end of time with the title, **The Imminent**; for all who deny that it is coming will never belie it when finally it happens. It takes its name from verse 1, which mentions "the Imminent Hour" (al-wāqiʿah) i.e., the Day og Resurrection. The surah whose central message is stated in its opening verses: the Day of Judgement is inevitable and it will sort people into the humiliated and the richly rewarded. As in the previous surah, people are divided into three classes: those brought near to God (the best of the believers), those on the right (the ordinary believers), and those on the left (the disbelievers). Ample proof is given of God's power and consequently His ability to bring about the Resurrection (verse 57 ff.).
The surah is also known as That Which is Coming, The Indisputable Event, The Inevitable, The Inevitable Event, The Occurrence, The Terror

1.1: That is, the Day of Resurrection and Judgement.

3.1: That is, abasing the faithless and raising the faithful in station.

13.1: That is, from the communities of the former prophets.

29.1: This is according to the reading _wa ṭalʿin manḍūd_ (instead of _wa ṭalḥin manḍūd_, meaning 'and clustered plantains') narrated from Imam ʿAlī and Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (_ʿa_) and Ibn ʿAbbās. (_Muʿjam_, _al-Kashshāf_).

75.3: Or 'by the places where the stars fall.' Or 'I swear by the orbits of the stars.'

82.1: Or 'livelihood.' According to the reading _tajʿalūna shukrakum_, narrated from Imam ʿAli ibn Abī Ṭālib and Imam al-Ṣādiq in _al-Tafsīr al-Qummī_ under this verse, the translation will be 'You make your denial of it your thanksgiving.' That is, instead of being grateful for it, you deny it.

83.1: That is, the soul, while leaving the body during the death-throes.

85.1: That is, to the dying person.

86.1: Or 'if you are not liable to retribution.'

88.1: That is, of 'the foremost ones' mentioned in verses <{["Q", "56:10"]}> - <{["Q", "56:11"]}>.

translations.2: —there is no denying that it will befall—
translations.4: When the earth is shaken violently,
translations.5: and the mountains are shattered into bits
translations.8: The People of the Right Hand —and what are the People of the Right Hand?
translations.9:
And the People of the Left Hand
 —and what are the People of the Left Hand?
translations.10: And the Foremost Ones are the foremost ones:<{["F", 1]}>
translations.11: they are the ones brought near [to Allah],
translations.12: [who will reside] in the gardens of bliss.
translations.14: and a few from the latter ones.
translations.16: reclining on them, face to face.
translations.17: They will be waited upon by immortal youths,
translations.18:
with goblets and ewers
   and a cup of a clear wine,<{["F", 1]}>
translations.19:
which neither causes them headache
     nor stupefaction,
translations.20: and such fruits as they prefer
translations.21: and such flesh of fowls as they desire,
translations.24: a reward for what they used to do.
translations.25:
They will not hear therein
   any vain talk or sinful speech,
translations.27:
And the People of the Right Hand
  —what are the People of the Right Hand?
translations.35: We have created them with a special creation,
translations.38: for the People of the Right Hand.
translations.40: and a multitude from the latter [ones].
translations.41:
And the People of the Left Hand
  —what are the People of the Left Hand?
translations.42: Amid infernal miasma and boiling water
translations.43: and the shadow of a dense black smoke,
translations.45: Indeed they had been affluent before this,
translations.46: and they used to persist in the great sin.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.47:
And they used to say,
 'What! When we are dead and become dust
   and bones,
  shall we be resurrected?
translations.50:
will all be gathered
   for the tryst of a known day.
translations.52: will surely eat from the Zaqqūm tree
translations.53: and stuff your bellies with it,
translations.54: and drink boiling water on top of it,
translations.56:
Such will be the hospitality they receive
  on the Day of Retribution.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.57:
We created you.
  Then why do you not acknowledge it?
translations.58: Have you considered the sperm that you emit?
translations.59:
Is it you who create it,
  or are We the creator?
translations.60:
We have ordained death among you,
 and We are not to be outmaneuvered
translations.61:
from replacing you with your likes
   and recreating you
    in [a realm] you do not know.
translations.62:
Certainly you have known the first genesis,
  then why do you not take admonition?
translations.63: Have you considered what you sow?
translations.64:
Is it you who make it grow,
  or are We the grower?
translations.65:
If We wish, We surely turn it into chaff,
 whereat you are left stunned<{["F", 1]}> [saying to yourselves,]
translations.68: Have you considered the water that you drink?
translations.69:
Is it you who bring it down from the rain cloud,
  or is it We who bring [it] down?
translations.70:
If We wish We can make it bitter.
 Then why do you not give thanks?
translations.71: Have you considered the fire that you kindle?
translations.72:
Was it you who caused its tree to grow,
  or were We the grower?
translations.73:
It was We who made it a reminder
  and a boon for the desert-dwellers.
translations.74: So _celebrate_ the Name of _your_ Lord, the All-supreme.
translations.75:
So I swear<{["F", 1]}>
  by the places where<{["F", 2]}> the stars set!<{["F", 3]}>
translations.76: And indeed it is a great oath, should you know.
translations.77: This is indeed a noble Qur'ān,
translations.79: —no one touches it except the pure ones—
translations.80: gradually sent down from the Lord of all the worlds.
translations.81: What! Do you take lightly this discourse?
translations.82: And make your denial of it your vocation?<{["F", 1]}>
translations.83: So when it<{["F", 1]}> reaches the throat [of the dying person]
translations.84: and at that moment you are looking on
translations.85:
—and We are nearer to him<{["F", 1]}> than you are,
   though you do not perceive—
translations.86: then why do you not, if you are not subject<{["F", 1]}>
translations.87:
[to the Divine dispensation], restore it,
    should you be truthful?
translations.88: Then, if he be of those brought near,<{["F", 1]}>
translations.89: then ease, abundance, and a garden of bliss.
translations.90: And if he be of the People of the Right Hand,
translations.91:
then 'Peace be on you,'
  [a greeting] from the People of the Right Hand!
translations.92:
But if he be of the impugners,
   the astray ones,
translations.93: then a treat of boiling water
translations.96: So _celebrate_ the Name of _your_ Lord, the All-supreme!
